title: True / False / Not Given
tips: Find the part of the passage that discusses the statement's topic, then compare meaning, not wording.
TRUE: the passage says the same thing in different words. FALSE: it says the opposite. NOT GIVEN: the passage never says it, even if it sounds likely.
Watch absolute words (all, only, always, never) and comparatives. One changed word usually makes a statement FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
Never use your own knowledge. If you cannot point to a sentence, it is NOT GIVEN.

title: Matching headings
tips: Read the first and last sentence of each paragraph first. The main idea is usually there.
A heading covers the whole paragraph. A detail that appears in one sentence is a trap.
Do the paragraphs with obvious headings first, then eliminate.

title: Completion and short answer
tips: Use the exact words from the passage and obey the word limit. A wrong word form loses the mark.
Predict the type of word first (noun, number, adjective), then scan for it.
Answers follow passage order inside the same question group.

title: Time: 60 minutes, 3 passages
tips: About 20 minutes per passage, including transferring answers. Spend less on passage 1 to bank time for passage 3.
Skim the passage for 2 minutes only. Read the questions closely and scan the text for each one.
Never leave a blank. There is no penalty for wrong answers.

title: Distractors and corrections
tips: Speakers often state a value, then correct it. The final value is the answer.
Read the questions in the preparation time and underline the key word. Expect it to be paraphrased.
If you miss one answer, let it go. Losing the next three is worse.

title: Spelling, numbers and format
tips: Spelling counts. Practise letter names and double letters (double-L). Check plurals and singular nouns after the gap.
Write numbers as digits and keep units out of the answer if the form already prints them.
Section 4 has no pause between questions. Follow the signpost words (firstly, however, another factor).

title: Task 1: the overview
tips: Intro: paraphrase the question in one sentence. Overview: two sentences on the biggest trend or contrast, no numbers.
Body paragraphs group similar data. Compare, do not list every number.
Select 4-6 key figures. Use approximations (about, nearly) correctly and keep tenses consistent with the dates.
Maps and processes: describe change and sequence, use passives, and still write an overview.

title: Task 2: position and development
tips: Answer every part of the question. State your position in the introduction and repeat it in the conclusion.
Two body paragraphs, each with one main idea, an explanation and a specific example. Depth beats number of ideas.
Plan for 5 minutes, write for 30, check for 5. Aim for 270-300 words.
Avoid memorised openings. Use accurate, flexible vocabulary rather than rare words you are unsure of.

title: Part 1 and Part 2
tips: Part 1: answer directly, then add a reason or example. Two or three sentences, not one word and not a speech.
Part 2: use the minute to write 4-5 keywords for the bullet points, then cover all four bullets and keep going for the full two minutes.
Use a past, present and conditional mix in your story to show grammatical range.

title: Part 3 and fluency
tips: Give a position, a reason, and an example or contrast. Use phrases such as 'It depends on', 'In some cases', 'One reason is'.
If you do not know a word, paraphrase and carry on. Hesitating to search for words costs fluency.
Self-correct naturally, but do not restart every sentence.
